inequalities.reason: NA is served for 6 objectives at E3, from 0.2 to 1.45. The wavelength side is the red arm's filter passband, served as a band (filter_ff01_595_31_32_passband, E3) rather than a peak, so a spot size is computable at each edge of it. What is missing is the other side of the inequality: a required lateral resolution, which is the question's to state and which this goal card does not. Its targets are decade_resolution on tracer_brightness, decade_resolution on bleaching_rate, and none of those is a length. Neither side is guessed (P5).

12 sample-plane pixel sizes at E2 measured on this instrument, 6 objective NAs at E3 and the red arm's passband at E3 are enough to compare a pixel against a diffraction-limited spot without back-deriving anything. 100x@1.5x pixel 0.04333 um against 0.0999-0.1053 um at NA 1.45; 100x@1x pixel 0.06500 um against 0.0999-0.1053 um at NA 1.45; 10x@1.5x pixel 0.43333 um against 0.3219-0.3392 um at NA 0.45; 10x@1x pixel 0.65000 um against 0.3219-0.3392 um at NA 0.45; 20x@1.5x pixel 0.21582 um against 0.1811-0.1908 um at NA 0.8; 20x@1x pixel 0.32373 um against 0.1811-0.1908 um at NA 0.8; 40x@1.5x pixel 0.10833 um against 0.1159-0.1221 um at NA 1.25; 40x@1x pixel 0.16250 um against 0.1159-0.1221 um at NA 1.25; 4x@1.5x pixel 1.08330 um against 0.7244-0.7631 um at NA 0.2; 4x@1x pixel 1.62500 um against 0.7244-0.7631 um at NA 0.2; 60x@1.5x pixel 0.07222 um against 0.1020-0.1075 um at NA 1.42; 60x@1x pixel 0.10833 um against 0.1020-0.1075 um at NA 1.42. 4 of 12 satisfy pixel <= lambda/(4*NA) at the band's short edge; 8 do not, and none is edge-dependent, so the band's width changes no verdict. **The permitted thing is the pair and not the pixel size**, which is why this is a set and not an interval: 0.10833 um appear with both verdicts, because the limit moves with NA. Magnification is not an input: these pixel sizes are measured at the sample plane, so nothing is divided by a magnification this instrument has never measured (5.3's 20.078x rule). Which pair the plan uses is S4's intersection with the pair the goal declares, not this axis's choice.

The instrument side is served: camera_sensor_geometry gives the sensor as 2400 by 2400 pixels, and the sample-plane pixel sizes are measured per objective-and-zoom pair, so the imaged field follows from those two without any magnification. `sensor_active_area` answers absent under that name and is not needed. What is missing is how much area has to be in frame at once, and that has to arrive on the goal card: how many tracers a measurement needs in view is A2's question, and 4.5.3 rule (b) forbids taking a sibling's output as input. It is not there.

This configuration runs with the spinning disk out -- the served entry states that with the disk out the same hardware serves widefield fluorescence and brightfield, and that disk-out is a required selector value on configurations that already exist rather than a configuration of its own. With the disk out there is no pinhole in the path, so there is no sectioning parameter for this bound to constrain. Recorded as not_constraining and not as no_input, and the difference is the next action: nothing to measure here, because the parameter does not exist on this configuration. What does not vanish with the pinhole is the out-of-focus light it would have rejected; that lands on depth_of_field below, which is where this axis carries it rather than dropping it.

The lenses on this turret sit in air, oil, water; an immersion index is served for air, water and not for oil. The 8 polystyrene indices that also came back are the tracer's material, not a medium a lens sits in, so they answer another question and are not a fallback at any grade. Even with every index and the band in hand this bound would not close here: its other side is how far a tracer wanders axially over the record, which depends on the record length, A2's parameter, and this axis does not take a sibling's output as input (4.5.3 rule b). So it states what is missing and leaves the intersection to S4.

note: The immersion indices arrived per medium and this axis reports which. Media with an index served: ['air', 'water']. Media an objective on this turret uses and no index answers for: ['oil']. So depth_of_field has its index for a lens in ['air', 'water'] and lacks it for one in ['oil'] -- which is what task 024 said to expect, because an immersion oil is a specific product's specification rather than a universal constant, and the bottle on this bench is not identified. What is missing is a source, not a measurement -- the same shape as the bead lot number. Answered by the librarian service rather than by reading the store, which is what makes degraded empty here: 36 entries came back with their own grades and 3 questions came back without one, all at the pinned kbv-4b981dc870d3, and every call is in librarian_agent/queries/log.jsonl under this caller_id. constraints[] is empty and there is one candidate it could have held: the NA set. It is six discrete values and `interval` can only say a continuous range, so returning it would license S4 to choose an NA of 0.9 that this nosepiece does not have. Abstaining is the honest outcome, and the contract gap is the same one A4 raised from the other side -- a bound with grounds that constrains something other than a number. Two axes met it independently; it is raised with manager-microscope, not worked around.
